articles.title: Which AI coding tools are actually worth using in 2026?
articles.excerpt: AI tools have gone from “cool autocomplete” to agents that can read a whole repo, edit multiple files and run commands. There are dozens now, so here’s how I’d think about it, plus a starter setup. Fi…
articles.body: AI tools have gone from “cool autocomplete” to agents that can read a whole repo, edit multiple files and run commands. There are dozens now, so here’s how I’d think about it, plus a starter setup. First, understand the three types Most confusion comes from comparing tools that do different jobs. Autocomplete and chat in your editor. It suggests the next line or function and answers questions about your code. It’s fast and low-risk, and it’s the easiest place to start. AI-first editors. The editor itself is built around AI, so you can say “change this behavior across these five files” and review a diff. Coding agents. You give them a goal (“migrate this module to the new API and fix the tests”), and they read the repo, edit files, run commands and iterate.

articles.title: Node.js Realtime Channel vs Polling: Logistics Notification Delivery Cost and Complexity
articles.excerpt: A dispatcher must know whether a driver is actually available before creating a video room and issuing a scoped token. That constraint changes the usual push-versus-polling answer: use a realtime chan…
articles.body: A dispatcher must know whether a driver is actually available before creating a video room and issuing a scoped token. That constraint changes the usual push-versus-polling answer: use a realtime channel for presence transitions, keep polling as reconciliation, and treat the database as the authority. A channel alone is fast but can preserve a false online state after a broken connection; polling alone makes presence accuracy depend on an interval. TL;DR: For a small logistics SaaS, the useful comparison is not request count versus socket count. It is the cost of being wrong about presence. Send compact, versioned presence events over a persistent channel, expire leases on the server, and poll a snapshot after reconnect or suspected gaps.

articles.title: Trail bird journal v1
articles.excerpt: What I Built Demo Code / Trail-Bird-Journal Trail Bird Journal An offline bird-song journal for your phone. Record or upload a clip, and the app identifies the birds with BirdNET and writes a short fi…
articles.body: What I Built Trail Bird Journal is an offline bird-song journal that runs entirely on my phone. You tap Record (or upload a clip), an open bird-sound model names the species it hears, and the app writes a short field-journal entry and saves it with the audio. A second page keeps a growing life list of every bird you've identified. It is for the person who walks past a hundred birds a day and has never known their names, and especially for the places where birdwatching actually happens: trails, woods and wetlands where there is no signal. A cloud app is useless there. This one works with airplane mode on, and your recordings never leave the phone. The point is to get you outside and keep you standing still.

articles.title: My spreadsheet-to-Markdown API taught me that 'the table' is a social construct — cells have opinions
articles.excerpt: I built the XLSX-to-Markdown converter expecting a spreadsheet to be a grid. Rows and columns. A nice Markdown table, maybe a JSON array beside it, done. That mental model lasted about three real-worl…
articles.body: I built the XLSX-to-Markdown converter expecting a spreadsheet to be a grid. Rows and columns. A nice Markdown table, maybe a JSON array beside it, done. That mental model lasted about three real-world workbooks. The first breakage: a financial model with a title row merged across A1:F1, a units row in row 2, actual headers in row 3, and totals three rows above the data they summarized. My converter faithfully emitted a Markdown table whose header row was "" | "" | "" | ..." and whose first data row was "Q1 Revenue (USD, thousands)" . Technically correct. Practically garbage for any agent downstream trying to parse it. The second breakage was worse.

articles.title: ScopePilot AI: An Evidence-First AI Copilot to Protect Freelancers From Scope Creep
articles.excerpt: The Problem: Scope Creep Is Costly INCLUDED — covered by the agreed scope. ADDITIONAL — appears to require work beyond the original agreement. CONFLICTING — conflicts with an existing requirement or c…
articles.body: The Problem: Scope Creep Is Costly Freelancers and independent developers often face a difficult situation: a project begins with an agreed scope, but new requests gradually expand the work without a clear discussion of additional time, cost, or expectations. The challenge is not simply saying no to a client. It is being able to explain, professionally and confidently, what was originally agreed upon and how a new request differs. That inspired me to build ScopePilot AI — an AI copilot designed to help freelancers make more informed, evidence-based decisions when project requirements change. What I Built ScopePilot AI compares an agreed project scope against a new client request and helps identify whether the request is: INCLUDED — covered by the agreed scope.

articles.title: PrivateDesk: Ask Your Office PDFs Anything, Answered Locally With Page Citations
articles.excerpt: What I Built PrivateDesk is a local document Q&A app for small professional offices: accountants, clinics, and small law firms. These offices sit on piles of PDFs (contracts, invoices, intake forms, p…
articles.body: What I Built PrivateDesk is a local document Q&A app for small professional offices: accountants, clinics, and small law firms. These offices sit on piles of PDFs (contracts, invoices, intake forms, policies) that they often cannot upload to a cloud AI tool because of client confidentiality. So they either skip AI completely or paste sensitive files into a service they don't control. PrivateDesk fixes that. You drop in your PDFs, ask a question in plain language ("What are the termination terms in the Sharma contract?"), and get an answer with the exact file name and page number it came from. A language model, embeddings, and the database all run on the office's own computer. It works with the Wi-Fi turned off.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 17, 2016: Private Antares rocket returns to flight after catastrophic launch explosion
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 17, 2016, the Antares rocket now built by Northrop Grumman Space Systems returned to flight to come back from a catastrophic explosion. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 17, 2016, Orbital ATK (now Northrop Grumman Space Systems ) returned to flight, successfully launching a cargo shipment to the International Space Station (ISS) after its previous cargo mission failed to launch. The private spaceflight company was contracted by NASA to fly cargo to the ISS, and stakes were high for this launch. Orbital ATK's last attempt nearly two years earlier ended in a catastrophic explosion a few seconds after liftoff. Despite some delays, the newly upgraded Antares rocket flawlessly blasted off into the night sky from NASA's Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia. Six days later, the Cygnus cargo spacecraft arrived at the ISS to deliver food, supplies and science experiments to the crew.

articles.title: The Orionid meteor shower peaks next week! Here's what to expect
articles.excerpt: The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, bringing a spectacular display of shooting stars to the autumn sky.
articles.body: The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, triggering a spectacular display of shooting stars as Earth plunges through the densest part of the debris trail shed by Halley's Comet. Here's what you need to know. When is the best time to see Orionid shooting stars? Orionid meteors are best spotted between the hours of midnight and dawn on Oct. 22, when 10-20 shooting stars may be seen brightening the night sky each hour under ideal dark-sky. The glare cast by the 74%-lit waxing gibbous moon will hide fainter shooting stars for much of the night. Thankfully, the lunar disk will set a few hours after midnight, leaving a window of beautifully dark sky before dawn in which to enjoy the full majesty of the annual meteor shower.

articles.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
